advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure overlap-judge (and post-verdict novelty/completion) LLM failures are recorded inside an active collect_step_failures() scope and drained onto coverage, since they currently run after produce_plan_review_verdict returns.
evidence: gate_dispatch.py:156-187 shows collect_step_failures() wraps only `_ex.run_workflow(...)`, which returns into `res` before produce_plan_review_verdict returns
overlap/judge.py:233-234: `except Exception: logger.warning("overlap judge batch call failed; treating as abstain", ...)` — the swallow site the feature intends to surface
step_failures.py record(): `sink = _step_failures.get(); if sink is None: return` — a no-op outside the scope
advisory.finding: The overlap-judge failures — the primary motivating case named throughout the commit message, module docstring, and schema description ('every overlap-judge batch dying') — are never captured, because overlap_findings runs in plan_review/__init__.py:770, AFTER gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict (called at __init__.py:615) has returned and thus after the collect_step_failures() scope (opened only around _ex.run_workflow in gate_dispatch.py:156-187) has exited and after drain() already ran in the plan_review_coach op. record() is a documented no-op outside an active sink, so these failures are silently dropped.
scenarios: Every overlap-judge batch fails (the observed live case: three batches, ~310s each): coverage.llm_step_failures is absent, exactly the byte-identical-to-clean outcome the ticket set out to eliminate.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the collect_step_failures() scope to cover the post-workflow floor/overlap section in plan_review/__init__.py (or open a nested scope there and merge its drain into coverage), so overlap_findings and _maybe_apply_rising_floor run under an active sink and their tally reaches coverage before validate_structured.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bring the post-verdict novelty/completion sub-call failures under an active step-failure sink so they are tallied like the docstring claims.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:190-191: `except Exception: logger.warning("rising-floor novelty scoring failed; running un-floored", exc_info=True)`
commit message / step_failures.py docstring: 'the novelty / contradiction / completion sub-calls degrade to "score nothing"' — cited as covered cases
scope of collect_step_failures() ends when produce_plan_review_verdict returns at line 615, before line 651 runs
advisory.finding: The novelty rising-floor sub-call's failures are also not captured for the same reason: _maybe_apply_rising_floor is invoked at plan_review/__init__.py:651, after produce_plan_review_verdict returned (line 615) and thus outside the collect_step_failures() scope and after drain(). Its fail-safe swallow ('running un-floored') is named in the commit/docstring as a target case but is never tallied.
scenarios: A remediation re-review where the novelty sub-call fails: it degrades to un-floored silently and the failure is not reflected in coverage.llm_step_failures.
